transcript.speaker: AI Interviewer
transcript.text: Hello Arjun! Welcome to your technical placement interview. I have reviewed your profile and projects. Let's start with a warm-up: could you give me a 60-second summary of your flagship project, CollabCode?

transcript.speaker: Arjun Sharma
transcript.text: Hi! CollabCode is a real-time collaborative code editor I built. It allows multiple developers to write, edit, and compile code in isolated docker containers together. I handled synchronization using WebSockets backed by Redis Pub/Sub so that typing latencies remain under 50 milliseconds across concurrent sessions.

transcript.speaker: AI Interviewer
transcript.text: Excellent. Let's dig deeper into the fundamentals. When two users type on the same line at nearly the exact same time, how does your system handle potential conflict resolution or race conditions?

transcript.speaker: Arjun Sharma
transcript.text: In our current prototype, we implemented an Operational Transformation (OT) lightweight queue where cursor movements and text operations carry a monotonic logical clock timestamp. Operations that arrive are applied sequentially on the server buffer before broadcasting to other connected sockets.

transcript.speaker: AI Interviewer
transcript.text: Good reasoning. What would happen if a client experiences a temporary network partition or 300ms packet loss and sends multiple buffered keystrokes all at once?

transcript.speaker: Arjun Sharma
transcript.text: The server checks the client's last acknowledged sequence number. If it detects a mismatch or stale state, it requests the client to rebase its pending operations against the authoritative server snapshot.

transcript.speaker: AI Interviewer
transcript.text: Let's touch on behavior: tell me about a time during HackMSOT when your team faced a blocking bug close to the submission deadline.

transcript.speaker: Arjun Sharma
transcript.text: With 45 minutes remaining, our Docker sandbox container was freezing due to unconstrained fork bombs. I quickly added a cgroup memory limit and process cap flag to the docker run command, allowing the container to fail gracefully without crashing the Node.js host. We demoed successfully and took 1st place.
